bracket: [Textbook misprint: the book's printed working sets \(l = 3\dfrac{\lambda}{2}\), which treats the string as fixed at BOTH ends — contradicting this example's own stem, where the string is fixed at one end and the vibrations are imposed at the FREE end. A free end is an antinode, so three complete loops are followed by a terminal quarter wavelength: \(l = \dfrac{7\lambda}{4}\), \(\lambda = 0.60\) m and \(\text{v} = 9.00\ \text{m s}^{-1}\), not the printed \(10.50\ \text{m s}^{-1}\). The book applies the correct treatment to the SAME configuration in Exercise Q.19 — a string fixed at one end, driven at 15 Hz at the free end — where it even prints the hint "Remember that the free end is an antinode", and its §6.5.3 says the same. The two are therefore inconsistent with each other and only Q.19 is right. The derivation above has been corrected.]
